Host claims form a stochastic process where each claim is a noisy observation of underlying player states. The injury claim process I(t) is modeled as a binary variable with probability p(I=1|C=c), where C represents claim confidence. Trade rumors T(t) evolve as a decayed Poisson process, with intensity R(t) = R_0 * exp(-λt). Fantasy picks P_i(t) are optimized using expected utility theory, assuming Gaussian rewards. Dualities emerge between claim reliability and player projection accuracy. Failure modes include false positives from unverified claims and overconfidence in early-season projections. Temporal consistency across shows acts as a regularizer for belief updates.
